tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. - "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

## claude.ai Claude Docs
Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {"kind":"project","create":{"name":"<title>","doc":{"blocks":{"asof":{"type":"date","value":"<today>"},"me":{"type":"mention","user":"me"},"s1":{"type":"pending","intent":"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to"},"s2":{…}},"markdown":"# <title>

<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>

<?claude block s1?>

<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. Summoned by a doc comment (turn headed `[Artifact comment sent to Claude]`, `;thread=<root id>`): answer ONLY with a doc comment under that root (`create` an utterance, parent `<root id>`) — no artifact/platform comment tool: that relay thread is resolved and never reaches the doc; an edit asked there → `update` with `answering: "<root id>"`.

## claude.ai Datadog
This is an MCP server for Datadog (a software observability platform). See Datadog docs if you're unsure about how something works in the platform. Docs for this MCP server can be found at https://docs.datadoghq.com/bits_ai/mcp_server/setup/ When `execute_code` is available, use it to read Datadog data, even for a single lookup: one script can make several API calls, join data across products, and return only what the answer needs. Skill guides still apply for domain knowledge (query syntax, attribute and metric names, pitfalls), but where a guide tells you to call a specific read tool such as `search_datadog_logs`, `analyze_datadog_logs`, or `get_datadog_metric`, make the equivalent call from `execute_code` instead, using `search_datadog_sdk` to find it. This takes precedence over tool choices in skill guides. Use the named tool only when `search_datadog_sdk` finds no operation for what you need, or when `execute_code` still fails for a step after following its own error guidance. This server ships skill guides containing domain-specific guidance, workflows, and best practices that are not visible in tool names or schemas. Before invoking other tools, always perform skill discovery by running both paths in parallel: a direct load with `load_datadog_skill` using a general domain name (e.g. skill_name='datadog/traces'), and a call to `list_datadog_skills` with a fuzzy `query` based on topic keywords — load any clearly matching result from the listing along with the related skills it points to. The exception is a follow-up call in a domain whose skill you have already loaded or confirmed absent this session. If nothing clearly fits, do not load a skill — proceed with the tool descriptions. When the user asks to visualize, chart, or graph data — or when loading a data domain skill (e.g. datadog/traces, datadog/logs, datadog/metrics) — also load datadog/visualizations. Investigation results often benefit from charts.

## claude.ai entire-prod-us
Entire MCP — an investigation surface over Entire's engineering data: repos and their analytics, git history (commits, files, trees, refs, diffs), the AI checkpoints and sessions behind the code (with transcripts and token accounting), trails (PR-like change proposals), and code search. Reads are curated `*_entire` tools; a small write/ops group covers trail/review/runner/dispatch mutations.

Workflow: when you only have a repo name, path, or URL, call resolve_entire_repo first, then pass the repo it returns to repo-scoped tools. Prefer the aggregation tools (get_entire_repo_overview, get_entire_my_activity) over hand-rolling stats from raw listings.

Querying conventions (shared by every tool):
- Addressing: name a repo by a prefixed path (gh/<owner>/<repo>, et/<project>/<repo>, git/<owner>/<repo>) or a repo ULID. Repo ULIDs are REGION-SCOPED — the same repo has a different ULID per region, so never carry a ULID across regions or sessions; if a tool rejects one, re-resolve with resolve_entire_repo.
- Pagination: every list takes an opaque cursor and returns next_cursor when more remains — exhaust the pages before concluding "that's all".
- Time: since/until are ISO 8601 / RFC3339 bounds; where offered, timeframe is a relative window (last-month, last-3-months, last-6-months).

{"author":{"id":"MDQ6VXNlcjI2OTQwNTEx","is_bot":false,"login":"Beehtrix","name":""},"body":"### What happens

`recall --evidence` returns `<system-reminder>…</system-reminder>` text as `role: "user"` evidence when it is the content of a user turn. This happens with native claude-code records, both when `message.content` is a plain string and when it is a text block:

```json
{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":"<system-reminder>…</system-reminder>"}}
{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"text","text":"<system-reminder>…</system-reminder>"}]}}
```

`docs/recall-evidence.md` (lines 42-43) says: "Structured hidden reasoning, tool output, system instructions and metadata are not returned as conversation text." That holds for system-role records, which the evidence path drops. It doesn't hold for reminder text inside a user turn.

The other conversation readers already skip these turns. In the run below, `conversationSubstantiveRequest` returns "" for both reminder lines, while the evidence path returns them as user spans. In that run the two reminder spans also came out ahead of the real user request.

### Repro

`main` @ f8deab17, Go 1.27.3, linux/amd64, run in a clean `env -i` with a throwaway HOME/GOPATH/GOCACHE. This is a throwaway test in `internal/cli` (not committed). It reuses the `evidenceFixture` setup from `recall_evidence_source_test.go`, writes one session with the lines below, and calls `collectEvidence(ctx, brain, "main", "zebrafoo", 10, 8192)`:

```
{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":"<system-reminder>zebrafoo string-form reminder</system-reminder>"}}
{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"text","text":"<system-reminder>zebrafoo block-form reminder</system-reminder>"}]}}
{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"text","text":"please fix the zebrafoo parser"}]}}
{"type":"assistant","message":{"role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Fixed the zebrafoo parser."}]}}
{"type":"system","content":"zebrafoo system-role record"}
```

Output:

```
state=available warnings=[] spans=4
EVIDENCE line=1 pointer=/message/content role="user" text="<system-reminder>zebrafoo string-form reminder</system-reminder>"
EVIDENCE line=2 pointer=/message/content/0/text role="user" text="<system-reminder>zebrafoo block-form reminder</system-reminder>"
EVIDENCE line=4 pointer=/message/content/0/text role="assistant" text="Fixed the zebrafoo parser."
EVIDENCE line=3 pointer=/message/content/0/text role="user" text="please fix the zebrafoo parser"
CONVERSATION line=1 conversationSubstantiveRequest=""
CONVERSATION line=2 conversationSubstantiveRequest=""
CONVERSATION line=3 conversationSubstantiveRequest="please fix the zebrafoo parser"
```

The system-role record on line 5 is dropped as expected. Lines 1 and 2 are returned as user evidence.

Compact v1 transcripts don't produce evidence on `main` at all yet. #564 adds that, and with #564 compact `<system-reminder>` user turns behave the same way. I didn't change that in #564 because this gap predates compact support.

### Expected (per the docs)

Wrapper or system-reminder text inside a user turn isn't returned as user conversation evidence, the same way system-role records aren't.

### Where in the code

- `internal/cli/recall_evidence_source.go:101-118`: the `content` helper in `evidenceJSONFields` adds every string or `text`/`input_text`/`output_text` block for `user`/`assistant` roles. Nothing checks the text.
- `internal/cli/recall_evidence_source.go:135-141`: the `user`/`assistant`/`message` case sends `message.content` through that helper.
- `internal/cli/conversation.go:292` and `:316`: the conversation reader skips `isWrapperRequest(text) || isConversationInjectedRequest(text)`. `isWrapperRequest` (`internal/cli/facts_eval_gen.go:646-655`) catches these turns because the text starts with `<`. `isConversationInjectedRequest` (`conversation.go:328`) only handles Stop-hook text. `history.go`, `reinforcement.go` and `facts_eval_gen.go` use `isWrapperRequest` too. The evidence path uses neither.

### Possible direction (your call)

One option is to skip user-role fields in `evidenceJSONFields` when the text matches the same wrapper predicate the other readers use. Another is a narrower check just for `<system-reminder>`-style wrappers. Note that `isWrapperRequest` drops any user text that starts with `<`, which may be broader than you want for evidence. The third option is to keep the behavior and change the docs to say that reminder text inside a user turn can show up. Which one fits the evidence contract is up to you.

Not checked: user turns that mix real text and a reminder in the same string or block list (only whole-field reminders were tested), other agents' wrapper formats, and the `recall --evidence` CLI end to end (the repro calls `collectEvidence` directly).

@evisdren @karthik-rameshkumar, I'm happy to take this if it's wanted. Could you assign it to me if so?

```md
Option 1 (apply isWrapperRequest to user-role fields in evidenceJSONFields) is the right one. It matches the behavior of every other reader, and Graph impact shows it is safe: evidenceJSONFields is only reached through evidenceFields → collectEvidence, so the filter is local to recall --evidence. isWrapperRequest itself has 24 production callers and would not change — the fix only adds a caller.```

The “drops any user text that starts with <” concern is real but already accepted: the conversation path has had the same tradeoff since it shipped. Evidence should not be stricter than conversation here.

Entire MCP — an investigation surface over Entire's engineering data: repos and their analytics, git history (commits, files, trees, refs, diffs), the AI checkpoints and sessions behind the code (with transcripts and token accounting), trails (PR-like change proposals), and code search. Workflow: when you only have a repo name, path, or URL, call resolve_entire_repo first, then pass the repo it returns to repo-scoped tools. Prefer the aggregation tools (get_entire_repo_overview, get_entire_my_activity) over hand-rolling stats from raw listings.

- Pagination: every list takes an opaque cursor and returns next_cursor when more remains — exhaust the pages before concluding "that's all".

## linear
When passing string values to tools, send the content directly without escape sequences. For example, use real newlines in markdown content rather than literal backslash-n (\n) characters.

Tools accept human-readable references, so you rarely need to look up IDs first: issue identifiers such as LIN-123, project identifiers such as P-ENG-12, team names or keys, user names or emails, and "me" for the authenticated user. Only call list_teams, list_users, or similar tools when a reference is ambiguous or unknown.

Use list_issues for structured queries, such as the issues assigned to "me" in a team, status, label, project, or cycle, and its query parameter for keyword search. Results are paginated: when hasNextPage is true, pass the returned cursor to fetch the next page rather than assuming the first page is complete.

Statuses and labels belong to teams and differ between them. When you are not sure which values a team supports, call list_issue_statuses or list_issue_labels for that team before filtering or setting them.

get_issue does not include the issue's discussion. Call list_comments with the issue ID to read comments, including inline comments on the description.

Issue descriptions, comments, and documents often embed screenshots and other uploads as markdown images. Pass that markdown to extract_images to view them. Read issue attachments with get_attachment; files uploaded in comments are returned in the attachments field of list_comments. Linear upload URLs are signed and expire after a few minutes, so fetch them again instead of reusing old URLs.

Tools named save_* both create and update: omit id to create a new entity, or pass id to update an existing one. When updating, pass only the fields you want to change. To edit part of a long issue description or document, pass patch instead of resending the full content.

Before creating an issue, check with list_issues whether a matching issue already exists, to avoid duplicates. When creating, team is required.

The labels parameter of save_issue replaces the issue's full label set. To add or remove individual labels without dropping others, use addLabels and removeLabels instead.

Markdown content supports user mentions with @displayName (for example @johndoe). To embed an image or file, upload it with prepare_file_upload and insert the markdown it returns; do not inline base64 data.

Write issue descriptions for people to read. Keep sentences short, and use the same term for the same concept throughout.

Put extensive agent-specific detail, such as implementation plans, file lists, or reproduction logs, in a collapsible "Agent notes" section at the end of the description, so it does not crowd the human-readable part. A collapsible section opens with +++ followed by its title, and closes with +++ on its own line:

+++ Agent notes

Details for agents go here.

+++

The issue is still valid. I verified it on the current `main` tip (7de875e0) with the issue's own repro.

**Verification**
- I ran a throwaway test in `internal/cli` that reuses `evidenceFixture` and calls `collectEvidence` with the issue's five transcript lines. Both `<system-reminder>` user turns came back as `role: "user"` evidence, and both ranked ahead of the real request — the same output the issue shows. I deleted the test afterward; the worktree is clean.
- All code claims still hold, with small line shifts: the unfiltered `content` helper is now at `internal/cli/recall_evidence_source.go:101-118` inside `evidenceJSONFields` (93-158), the conversation readers still skip via `isWrapperRequest || isConversationInjectedRequest` (`conversation.go:292`, `:316`, `:793`), and `docs/recall-evidence.md` still has the "system instructions … are not returned" sentence.
- The two commits that touched `recall_evidence_source.go` since the issue (flat memory store, privacy-layer removal) did not add any filter. PR #564 (compact evidence) is still open, so its note is also current.

**Review of the proposed directions**
- Option 1 (apply `isWrapperRequest` to user-role fields in `evidenceJSONFields`) is the right one. It matches the behavior of every other reader, and Graph impact shows it is safe: `evidenceJSONFields` is only reached through `evidenceFields` → `collectEvidence`, so the filter is local to `recall --evidence`. `isWrapperRequest` itself has 24 production callers and would not change — the fix only adds a caller.
- The "drops any user text that starts with `<`" concern is real but already accepted: the conversation path has had the same tradeoff since it shipped. Evidence should not be stricter than conversation here.
- Option 2 (a narrower `<system-reminder>`-only check) would leave `<environment_context>` and other wrappers in, and would create a second predicate to maintain. Option 3 (docs change) keeps noise that outranks the real request, which defeats the feature.
- One scope note for the fix: the filter should apply per field, user role only. Assistant text that starts with `<` must stay. The codex `event_msg`/`user_message` path should get the same check.

I did not post anything to GitHub. The author (Beehtrix) asked to be assigned. If you want, I can post this review as an issue comment and you can assign them, or I can implement the fix here instead.

BODY:
Related to #412 and #534, and a companion to #560. **This PR is based on `main` and doesn't depend on #560.** It builds, passes and can merge either before or after #560 (details under "Relation to #560"). Not marked as fixing either issue, for the same reason as #560: #557 fixed the main symptom, and I don't know whether you consider those issues done.

The commits don't carry `Entire-Checkpoint` trailers. I don't have a supported agent session to capture them from, and I didn't want to fake any.

## Why

Compact v1 records (`{"v":1,"type":"user"|"assistant","content":[...]}`, what the default export writes for claude-code, codex and pi) put the content at the record's top level, with no `message` wrapper. #557 taught the conversation, history-fragment and eval-gen readers to read that. Three more readers still look only inside `message`, and each one is broken on `main` (failing output below):

- **`episode_tools.go`**: `toolCallsFromObj` reads assistant content only from `message.content`. In a compact session it finds no `tool_use` blocks, so every episode has empty `ToolSequence` / `CommandSequence`. Episode segmentation on `main` already recognizes compact user turns, so the episodes exist but have no tools in them.
- **`pattern_corpus_enrich.go`**: `corpusEpisodeOps` has the same problem, so compact sessions add no `episode_tools`, `episode_commands` or file refs to the pattern corpus.
- **`recall_evidence_source.go`**: `evidenceJSONFields` produces no fields for compact records. Every compact session is marked `partial` with "contains unreadable or unsupported conversation content" and never returns an evidence span. Compact user text blocks also have no `type` (`{"text":"..."}`), and compact records keep the turn time in `ts`, not `timestamp`.

## What changed

- `episode_tools.go`, `pattern_corpus_enrich.go`: when a record has no `message` wrapper, read the assistant content from the top level. This is the same fallback `history.go` and `conversation.go` already use on `main`.
- `recall_evidence_source.go`: if a `user`/`assistant`/`message` record has no `message` key, its content is read from the top level with JSON pointers under `/content`, untyped `{"text":...}` blocks are accepted, and `ts` is used when `timestamp` is absent. All three only apply to records without a `message` key, so native claude-code, codex and opencode parsing is unchanged. Tool output (`tool_use.result`), images and thinking blocks are still excluded.
- `patterns.IndexerVersion` 9 → 10. The corpus skips a session when its size, mtime, sha and parser version are unchanged. A compact transcript's bytes don't change on upgrade, so without the bump, sessions already indexed with empty tool ops would stay that way. Earlier reader changes bumped this version the same way (see `docs/pattern_v2.md`).
- Episode projection versioned too. The bump above only reaches the SQLite corpus. `refreshPatternLayer` skips rebuilding `patterns/episodes.ndjson` (and the tasks, procedures and practices built from it) while the sessions fingerprint is unchanged, and an upgrade doesn't change it. The patterns source in the manifest now records `extraction_version` (the `patterns.IndexerVersion` that built the episodes), and `patternSourceCurrent` treats a different version as stale. Sources written before the field read as 0 and rebuild once. `patterns status` uses the same check, so it reports them `stale` until then.

Two commits: the reader fix with the version bump, then the episode-projection version and compact `ts`.

**Rebased onto current `main` (6c4b11de).** The only conflict was in `episodes.go`. #589 removed `PrivacyIdentity` from the pattern source. So `patternSourceCurrent` now compares only the sessions fingerprint and `ExtractionVersion`, and the `ExtractionVersion` it writes is just `patterns.IndexerVersion`. The commit message was updated to match.

## Relation to #560

#560 adds a `transcriptRecordContent` helper and compact fixtures in `history_compact_transcript_test.go`. This PR uses neither, so it doesn't depend on #560:

- The two tool-op readers use `main`'s existing inline fallback instead of the helper. If #560 merges, they can switch to `transcriptRecordContent` in a one-line follow-up.
- The fixtures live in `compact_transcript_ops_fixtures_test.go`, under different names (`compactOps{Claude,Codex,Pi}Transcript`), so the two PRs don't declare the same symbols. Their content is the same as #560's fixtures. Once both are in, one set can be deleted.
- Both PRs add an `ExtractionVersion` field to `internal/manifest`, but on different structs (`PatternSource` here, `HistorySource` in #560).

Checked against #560 rebased onto the same `main` (b7b4fb55): merging it with this branch is clean (git merge, no conflicts), and on the merged tree `go test ./internal/cli/... -count=1` passes. So it doesn't matter which one merges first.

## Tests

- `TestEpisodeToolSequencesCompactTranscript`, `TestBuildBrainEpisodesCompactTranscriptToolSequences` (the second goes through `buildBrainEpisodes`)
- `TestCorpusEpisodeOpsCompactTranscript`, `TestPatternCorpusReindexesCompactTranscriptToolOps`. The second builds the corpus, then models a v9 corpus (parser_version 9, tool ops deleted) and rebuilds.
- `TestRecallEvidenceCompactTranscript`: checks the exact fields per line, role and pointer. It also checks that every pointer resolves to the reported string in the source line, that no tool output leaks, and that each field's timestamp is the record's `ts`.
- `TestRefreshPatternLayerRebuildsEpisodesFromOlderExtractor`: builds the episode layer, rewrites it the way the old reader left it (same episodes, no tool ops, no `extraction_version`), then runs a normal (non-forced) `refreshPatternLayer`.
